preregistration.decision_rule: A method is controlled on an unrelated condition when the Wilson 95% lower bound of its rate of declared relationships is at most alpha, and inflated when that bound exceeds alpha. A detection rate is the rate of declared relationships on a related condition. Abstentions are never counted as declared relationships. Hypotheses are evaluated on held-out conditions only. The rule, conditions, seeds, trial counts, methods, thresholds, and hypotheses were fixed before the held-out conditions were first run and are not changed after the rows are seen.

hypotheses.statement: The phase-synchrony test is controlled on every stationary unrelated held-out condition, including the phase-randomized negative control and independent oscillators at identical or harmonically related frequencies.
Each conventional baseline with a textbook threshold (Pearson correlation, Welch coherence, Rayleigh phase-locking value) is inflated on at least one stationary unrelated held-out condition.
On every held-out harmonic coupling (1:2 and 2:3), the phase-synchrony test detects the relationship at least 0.25 more often than existing DRR rooting.
The ratio search carries H3: with the ratio fixed at 1:1 the phase test detects each held-out harmonic coupling in at most 15% of trials.
The seam correction is load-bearing: without it the phase test is inflated on the held-out coherent identical-frequency condition, where the corrected test is controlled.
Existing DRR rooting is inflated on the held-out coherent identical-frequency condition.
Without the gate, the phase-synchrony test is inflated on the held-out shared-sweep condition, because its stationarity assumption fails there.
The data-quality gate abstains in at least 80% of trials on the held-out random walks and shared sweep, and in at most 10% of trials on every stationary held-out condition.
On the stationary held-out 1:1 couplings, the phase-synchrony test's mean detection rate is no more than 0.10 below existing DRR rooting's.

hypotheses.rule: phase_sync is controlled on every stationary unrelated condition
hypotheses.statement: The phase-synchrony test is controlled on every stationary unrelated held-out condition, including the phase-randomized negative control and independent oscillators at identical or harmonically related frequencies.

hypotheses.rule: each of pearson_analytic, coherence_analytic, plv_rayleigh is inflated on at least one stationary unrelated condition
hypotheses.statement: Each conventional baseline with a textbook threshold (Pearson correlation, Welch coherence, Rayleigh phase-locking value) is inflated on at least one stationary unrelated held-out condition.

hypotheses.rule: phase_sync detection rate minus drr_rooting detection rate >= 0.25 on every harmonic condition
hypotheses.statement: On every held-out harmonic coupling (1:2 and 2:3), the phase-synchrony test detects the relationship at least 0.25 more often than existing DRR rooting.

hypotheses.rule: phase_sync_1to1 detection rate <= 0.15 on every harmonic condition
hypotheses.statement: The ratio search carries H3: with the ratio fixed at 1:1 the phase test detects each held-out harmonic coupling in at most 15% of trials.

hypotheses.rule: phase_sync_no_seam is inflated and phase_sync controlled on the coherent condition
hypotheses.statement: The seam correction is load-bearing: without it the phase test is inflated on the held-out coherent identical-frequency condition, where the corrected test is controlled.

hypotheses.rule: drr_rooting is inflated on the coherent condition
hypotheses.statement: Existing DRR rooting is inflated on the held-out coherent identical-frequency condition.
Without the gate, the phase-synchrony test is inflated on the held-out shared-sweep condition, because its stationarity assumption fails there.

hypotheses.rule: gate abstention >= 0.8 on random_walk and common_chirp and <= 0.1 on every stationary condition
hypotheses.statement: The data-quality gate abstains in at least 80% of trials on the held-out random walks and shared sweep, and in at most 10% of trials on every stationary held-out condition.

hypotheses.rule: mean phase_sync detection rate on the stationary 1:1 couplings is at least the mean drr_rooting rate minus 0.10
hypotheses.statement: On the stationary held-out 1:1 couplings, the phase-synchrony test's mean detection rate is no more than 0.10 below existing DRR rooting's.

coherence_analytic.description: Welch magnitude-squared coherence at the first channel's peak, threshold (1 - C)^(K - 1) for K segments

coherence_shift.description: the same coherence against every circular shift of the second channel

drr_plus_phase.description: related if drr_rooting or phase_sync is significant at alpha / 2 (Bonferroni)

drr_plus_phase_gated.description: drr_plus_phase, abstaining when the data-quality gate abstains

drr_rooting.description: lagged correlation, lags 1-4, 99 circular-shift surrogates, max-statistic correction

drr_rooting_te.description: the same test with the transfer-entropy backend (pyinform)

oriented_area.description: normalized oriented area against every circular shift, two-sided

pearson_analytic.description: Pearson correlation at lag 0, Fisher z test assuming independent samples

phase_sync.description: n:m phase-locking value, Farey ratio search, exact seam-corrected shift test

phase_sync_1to1.description: phase_sync with the ratio fixed at 1:1

phase_sync_broadband.description: phase_sync on the Hilbert phase of the unfiltered series

phase_sync_gated.description: phase_sync, abstaining when the data-quality gate abstains

phase_sync_no_seam.description: phase_sync without the seam-correcting phase ramp

plv_rayleigh.description: 1:1 phase-locking value with the Rayleigh threshold exp(-N PLV^2) assuming independent samples

runtime.note: Wall-clock seconds per trial on the generating machine; not reproducible.
